name: Computer-use agent inference provider
one_line: An OpenAI-compatible endpoint serving an open VLM at a screenshot-sized visual-token budget behind a telemetry/dedup/affinity gateway, hosted or BYOC, whose only measured advantages are the model's own tokenizer arithmetic and prefix caching vLLM already ships; the product claim ($/completed CUA task at held accuracy) is unmeasured.
evidence_grade_reason: The claim a buyer pays for (lower $/completed CUA task at held accuracy) has never been measured on any CUA suite; no screenshot grounding number exists at the 312-322-token budget. What is measured is either a deterministic formula output (token counts from pricing.py, whose comparators are stale), a document benchmark at a different budget (DocVQA 0.925 at 1,017 tokens), a single synthetic 15-step trajectory (redundancy), a bounded/falsified encoder-reuse ceiling (~2.3x, n=8 frames, mRoPE-blocked), or vLLM prefix caching on a text model, single request, in-GPU, which the repo itself calls table stakes. The two gateway mechanisms that would be Dexa's own (exact-dup cache, session affinity) are respectively near-inert as coded and unbuilt. The "~40x" is a price model on an assumed $0.20/MTok rate. Grade D rather than C because the measured items are inputs to the thesis, not the thesis.
build_cost_weeks_to_proof: 7-9 weeks to the first credible public proof (a $/completed-task and success page on WebArena or Odysseys with 5 seeds, 5 backends, 2 screen sizes, published trajectories and per-request usage). Assumptions: one engineer full-time; the existing gateway/backend/compose reused as-is with the len/4 estimator replaced by vLLM usage fields; ~60-100 GPU-hours for the suite runs (~$150-250 at Modal A100 $2.50/h) plus ~30 GPU-h for the multi-replica affinity test and ~20 GPU-h for A100/H100 throughput; a Sonnet 5 API arm (unmeasured spend, on the order of hundreds of dollars for 100-200 tasks x 5 seeds); browser/VM infrastructure for the suite; harness bring-up taking 1-2 weeks (the most likely slip); kill gate 1 (grounding at the capped budget) reviewed at week 2-3 before any affinity work. If OSWorld-Verified is chosen instead of a browser suite, add 1-2 weeks for desktop VM infrastructure and a desktop agent harness. No design partners exist, so pilot-derived proof is not in this window.

attacks.attack: The proof benchmark as drafted cannot isolate a Dexa advantage. At 1280x800 the budget cap is inert (322 tokens capped or uncapped, reproduced this session), so baseline (1) (same model on vanilla vLLM) is token-identical to Dexa; the only Dexa-specific levers left are the exact-dup cache (near-inert as coded) and session affinity (unbuilt). A well-configured vLLM/SGLang baseline with prefix caching therefore matches Dexa on cost and latency at the screen size the redundancy bench used.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Run the benchmark at two screen sizes and publish both arms: 1280x800 (expected parity with baseline (1); labeled gateway-only) and 1920x1080 where the cap bites (646 -> 312 tokens). If the 1080p arm shows success within 3 points of native resolution and lower $/task, the budget lever is real; if it drops more than 8 points, the product reduces to hosting plus telemetry.

attacks.attack: Grounding accuracy at the served budget is unmeasured and the closest data points against it. The only accuracy measurement is DocVQA parity at 1,017 tokens per page; on the same document sweep 512px (277 tokens) lost 20 points and 384px (182) lost 49. The screenshot budget (312-322 tokens) sits between the 512px and 768px document points, and a 1080p screen under the cap is rendered at ~0.69x linear scale, shrinking UI text.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: WebArena/Odysseys (or OSWorld with its desktop harness) task success, same model, native vs capped, 5 seeds, both screen sizes; plus a ScreenSpot-style click-grounding accuracy at 312 and 322 tokens vs native. Kill line pre-registered at > 8 points absolute drop.

attacks.attack: The modeled price gap collapses against current comparators. pricing.py compares to gpt-4o ($2.50, tile rule) and 'claude-3-5-sonnet' ($3/$15, w*h/750 rule); re-based on documented rules and list prices the gap is ~30x vs Sonnet 5, ~35x vs gpt-5.4, but only ~3.7x vs gpt-5.6-luna/gpt-5.4-nano ($0.20/MTok, 1,200 tokens), ~3.3x vs Gemini 3 low (280 tokens at $0.75), ~1.3-2.6x vs DeepSeek v4-flash-vision (384 tokens at $0.22-0.44), and ~1x vs hosted Qwen3-VL-8B at $0.20. The telemetry headers the product ships would compute savings against stale models.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Refresh PRICES and token rules in pricing.py, then measure $/completed task at equal success against hosted Qwen3-VL-8B, Sonnet 5, and (founder's choice) Gemini 3 low and DeepSeek vision arms. The 'Qwen host with telemetry' kill gate (within 1.5x of hosted Qwen) is the settling number.

attacks.attack: The exact-frame cache is near-inert as coded. It fires only when the frame is byte-identical to the previous frame AND the concatenated message text hash matches (app.py line 209). In an append-only OpenAI-compatible loop the text changes every step, and the redundancy bench's own data shows even type/edit actions change 2.5-6% of pixels, so consecutive frames are not byte-identical. Its only exerciser fabricates an identical frame every third step.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Replay recorded real trajectories through the gateway and report served_from_cache with the current key and with a last-frame-only key; pre-registered kill at < 3% of steps for both keys.

attacks.attack: Session affinity's value is bounded and unmeasured under the conditions that matter. The 12x/25-34x TTFT numbers are a text model, single request, in-GPU cache hit (no transfer), which the repo itself calls table stakes. The cacheable CUA prefix is only the static block because --limit-mm-per-prompt image:3 rotates screenshots out of history; the per-step upside is bounded by that block's cold prefill (~280 ms at 4k on A100). The hosted backend scales to zero after 300 s (min_containers=0), which discards the prefix cache on every cold start; multi-replica behavior is unmeasured and the router is unbuilt.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Consistent-hash router across >= 4 vLLM replicas; measure usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens share and TTFT with and without affinity on recorded CUA trajectories, including cold-start rate under scale-to-zero; kill at < 10 points gain or > 5% cold-start steps.

attacks.attack: The token advantage is the model's, not Dexa's, and a model swap can erase it. 322 tokens per 1280x800 frame is Qwen2.5-VL's smart-resize geometry; the founder-decision list includes Qwen3-VL-8B and Browser Use's 30B-A3B, and no research file records their per-image token counts. If the swap lands near 1,000 tokens per frame, the 3.4-4.1x token lever disappears while the pricing telemetry still reports it.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Measure per-frame visual tokens from vLLM usage for each candidate model on the same 1280x800 and 1080p frames; kill at >= 1,000 per 1280x800 frame.

attacks.attack: The 6-week plan slips on the harness, not the gateway. Week 1 assumes a working WebArena/OSWorld harness wired to two agent frameworks plus recorded trajectories; the draft also mixed browser harnesses with a desktop suite they cannot run. 5 seeds x 5 backends x 2 screen sizes x 100-200 tasks is 5,000-10,000 task executions dominated by browser/VM wall-clock, and the Sonnet 5 arm needs API budget. The voice harness slated for the throughput test sends synthetic token ids and has no text, tokenizer, chat endpoint or image path. 'Design-partner pilots' in Week 6 have no contacts behind them.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: A Week 1 gate: 20 tasks run end-to-end on two backends with usage fields captured by day 5; otherwise re-plan to 8-9 weeks. Rename Week 6 to outreach.

attacks.attack: 'Proven' items are formula outputs or single-trajectory synthetic measurements. The token accounting is deterministic code (5 unit tests) with stale comparators; the redundancy numbers come from one 15-step Playwright CRM task with a 180 ms harness wait, not OSWorld/WebArena frames; the tolerance-sweep ceiling is n = 8 frames with grounding tolerance never tested; the DocVQA parity is 200 pages, relaxed match, at a different budget. None of these survives as production evidence without the suite run.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: The section 6 Unproven table: suite success at budget (5 seeds), exact-dup hit rate on real trajectories, prefix-hit rate across replicas, steps per GPU-hour on A100/H100, per-frame tokens per candidate model.

attacks.attack: Real $/step is unmeasured; the only throughput point is documents (30.2 pages/s at 1,017 tokens on one A100) turned into a hardcoded '$0.02-0.06 / 1k pages' at an assumed $1.80/GPU-h. The pricing options in section 8 cannot be set and the '<= 0.5x hosted Qwen at 50% utilization' proceed line is a guess until steps/GPU-hour exists.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Load test at the CUA budget on A100 and H100 with p95 step latency <= 2 s; publish steps per GPU-hour and implied $/MTok-equivalent.

attacks.attack: Version and packaging drift. The backend is pinned to vLLM 0.24.0 (0.28.0 is current) and depends on version-specific multimodal CLI flags; the BYOC Dockerfile omits control/, so the image cannot run accounts or the credit gate; no integration test against a live backend exists in-repo.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Run docker-compose.byoc.yml on current vLLM on a rented A100/H100 with control/ included; pass a smoke test through the gateway with usage fields.

attacks.attack: Workload assumptions the research files do not support: the brief assumes a one-screenshot-per-step loop with a static prefix and short actions, and prices per step, but no file records CUA turn timing, idle gaps, concurrency, screen sizes or history length; the coding-agent analogs (Mooncake, TraceLab) are text workloads.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Record timing, screen size, history length and images-per-request from the Week 1 trajectories and publish them alongside the benchmark.

missing_founder_decisions: Suite and harness pairing: WebArena/Odysseys with Browser Use or Skyvern vs OSWorld-Verified with a desktop agent harness (the draft combined browser harnesses with a desktop suite they cannot run); success definition and the seed count that counts as proof.
Screen-size policy: cap 1080p+ screens to ~312 tokens (cheaper, grounding unmeasured, ~0.69x linear scale) or serve native (646-1,196 tokens, no budget advantage); the draft silently chose the cap.

Whether a 'Qwen host with telemetry' outcome is acceptable: the draft's kill line (within 1.5x of hosted Qwen3-VL-8B) encodes a judgment that reselling a hosted open VLM with BYOC and telemetry is not a business; that is the founder's call, not a measurement.
Whether to re-key the exact-dup cache to the last frame only (ignoring history text), accepting the correctness risk that an identical frame with new history may deserve a new answer.
Hosted scale-to-zero (current Modal config) vs always-warm replicas: cost per idle hour vs prefix-cache warmth and cold-start latency.

Which comparators and prices the telemetry publishes (pricing.py's stale gpt-4o/claude-3-5-sonnet rows vs re-based gpt-5.4/Sonnet 5/luna/nano) and whether buyers set their own baseline table via x-dexa-baseline.

Whether frontier small-image modes (Gemini 3 low 280 tokens, DeepSeek 384 tokens, gpt-5.6-luna/gpt-5.4-nano at $0.20/MTok) are benchmark arms; their derived per-frame cost is 1.3-3.7x Dexa's assumed cost, not ~40x.
Model choice including a CUA-trained model (Browser Use 30B-A3B) vs a general VLM, with the per-frame token count re-measured for each because the 322-token figure is Qwen2.5-VL-specific.
Build ordering: whether to build the affinity router and streaming before or after kill gate 1 (the draft built affinity in Week 3 regardless of the grounding result).
Which buyer segment to approach first for design partners (QA/RPA teams, browser-agent framework users, enterprise VPC deployments); no customer contact exists in any file.
Pricing unit (per step vs per token vs $0-cached) and whether to license the BYOC recipe plus telemetry separately from hosted inference.
strongest_version: The strongest honest form is a benchmark-first BYOC/hosted endpoint for screenshot agents whose pitch is verifiable per-step economics rather than a novel engine: an open VLM whose tokenizer bills 322 tokens for a 1280x800 frame against 1,105-1,334 on frontier tokenizers, served on stock vLLM with prefix caching, behind a gateway that reports observed (not modeled) per-step cost against the buyer's chosen baseline and keeps screenshots inside the customer's VPC. Its proof is a published $/completed-task page on a browser suite with five seeds, five backends and two screen sizes, where the 1280x800 arm openly shows parity with vanilla vLLM and the 1080p arm tests whether the visual-token cap holds grounding. If that gate passes, the defensible additions are session-affinity routing measured by cached_tokens across replicas and a re-keyed duplicate-frame cache, priced per step; if it fails, the product is a hosted/BYOC open-VLM endpoint with telemetry at roughly hosted-Qwen prices, which the founder may still choose to pursue. The delta-perception engine remains a separately gated R&D bet with a measured ~2.3x ceiling and an mRoPE blocker.
